  "text": "The laundrette installed a lost-property machine beside the dryers.

INSERT ONE COIN, the label said. RECOVER WHAT YOU HAVE LOST.

I expected socks.

For fifty pence, it returned the blue mitten I'd dropped in a canal when I was six. It was still wet.

The attendant watched me through the glass of her office.

“Only once a week,” she said.

The next Friday, I tried again.

A tooth rattled into the tray. Not a baby tooth. The molar my father had lost in the accident that killed him.

I knew because of the gold crown.

“That isn't mine,” I told her.

“Was he?”

I put it in my pocket.

All week, I felt it knocking against my keys, though I had left it in a drawer.

On Friday, I brought every coin in the flat.

The attendant locked her office when she saw me.

First came his watch.

Then his wedding ring.

Then a folded shopping list, with bread underlined twice.

The machine grew warm.

I fed it another coin.

Something heavy struck the tray from inside.

“Stop,” the attendant said through the door.

I knelt. Behind the flap, someone was breathing.

“Dad?”

A finger pushed through. It wore his ring, although the ring was in my hand.

“Another coin,” he whispered.

My purse was empty.

The attendant wouldn't open her door. I searched beneath every washer and dryer, scraping lint from the floor.

Behind me, the flap clicked shut.

When I returned to the machine, its label had changed.

INSERT ONE COIN, it said. RETURN WHAT YOU HAVE FOUND.

From my pocket came a small, patient knock."
